title: Ride-sourcing clarified as legal (Tasmania)
summary: The Taxi and Hire Vehicle Industries Amendment Act 2016 clarified that ride-sourcing providers could operate in Tasmania under existing hire-vehicle requirements and let the Minister suspend annual releases of new taxi licences.

instruments.title: Taxi and Hire Vehicle Industries Amendment Act 2016
instruments.provisions: Amends Taxi and Hire Vehicle Industries Act 2008

direction_rationale: Legalising app-based ride-share removes the legal barrier to entry created by taxi/hire-car licence quotas, adding a new type of supplier and price competition in point-to-point transport. The same Act allowed suspension of new taxi licence releases (a partial offset).
comparison: States that had not yet legalised ride-sharing (ACT Oct 2015 first, NT Dec 2017/Feb 2018 last)
confounders: taxi licence compensation and per-trip levies
ABN registration by gig drivers inflates business counts
notes: Actual Uber launch date in Hobart not verified.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Legalised app-based ride-share alongside taxis, removing the barrier that capped taxi and hire-car licences placed on point-to-point transport. Nationally, businesses in taxi and other road transport rose from about 16,000 in June 2015 to about 39,500 in June 2019 as drivers joined (ABS business counts).

marks.reason: Legal ride-sourcing adds suppliers, though the same Act let the Minister suspend new taxi licence releases.
Legalises app-based booking and pricing across the industry.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation could not identify the effect on business entry, because ride-share drivers are counted with taxis and the data changed at the same time.
